notes:
I couldn't write these notes. The research tools stopped working before I could read any of the sources.

My first attempt tried to load seven pages at once: Enduring Word, Bible Hub's Ezekiel 2:1 page, the Gill, Ellicott and Pulpit Commentary pages, Precept Austin and the NET Bible notes. That went over the tool's usage limit. When I retried with just the Enduring Word page, the tool said I had no calls left for this turn. So I read nothing for Ezekiel 2.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. Because of that, I haven't written any verse notes. Anything I wrote now would come from memory, with no page behind it.

**Next time I'd start with these pages:**
- Traditional reading: Enduring Word on Ezekiel 2, then Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub or StudyLight, and Precept Austin's Ezekiel 2 commentary.
- Where Protestant traditions differ: Wesley's Notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Ligonier, The Gospel Coalition and Desiring God. I'd look especially at v. 2 (the Spirit entering the prophet) and vv. 5–7 (being faithful whether people listen or not).
- Other views: the NET Bible notes for v. 1 ("son of man") and v. 10 (a scroll written on both sides); New Advent, Catholic.com and OCA for Catholic and Orthodox readings. I'd include popular modern teaching only if those sites actually discuss it for this chapter.

If you ask again in a new message, I'll start with one source at a time so I don't hit the limit. The full verse-by-verse notes may take a few rounds.
